title: Different strokes
goals: Describe lifestyles with adjectives (exciting, stressful, relaxing, unhealthy, boring, green).
Say what is happening now or in this period with the present continuous.

Understand and say numbers: ages, times, phone numbers, years, dates and amounts of money.

learn.title: Present continuous
learn.html:
We use the present continuous to talk about what is happening right now or in this period. Form: subject + be (am / is / are) + verb with -ing.

AffirmativeNegativeQuestionShort answer
I am working. (I'm)I'm not working.Am I working?Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
He/She/It is working.He/She/It isn't working.Is he working?Yes, he is. / No, he isn't.
You/We/They are working.You/We/They aren't working.Are they working?Yes, we are. / No, we aren't.

Question words: Wh- + be + subject + verb-ing (What are you doing? Where is he working?).

Spelling of -ingExamples
Normal: add -ingwait → waiting, play → playing, study → studying
Ends in -e: drop the etake → taking, write → writing, live → living
One syllable, consonant-vowel-consonant: double the consonantrun → running, swim → swimming, stop → stopping

Time expressions: now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, this semester, these days.

watch.wrong: The boy is play with a dog.
watch.right: The boy is playing with a dog.
Are you working? Yes, I am.
watch.why: The short affirmative answer is not contracted.

learn.title: Present continuous vs. present simple
learn.html:
Present simplePresent continuous
Habits, routines, things that are always true or permanentWhat is happening now or in this period
I usually work for two months every summer.I'm working at the park at the moment.
Raoul usually plays squash three times a week.Albert is working very hard on his project today.
What do you do? (what is your job?)What are you doing? (what are you doing now?)
  • Clues for the simple: every day, usually, always, often, three times a week.
  • Clues for the continuous: now, right now, at the moment, today, this week.

State verbs: we do not use them in the continuous. They express feelings (like, love, hate, need), thoughts (know, think, want, understand, mean), senses (see, hear, smell, taste) and possession (belong, have = own).

I love my job. / She doesn't know Ben. But have as an activity can use the continuous: They are having a picnic.

watch.why: State verbs do not go in the continuous.
Know is a state verb: present simple.
We use the present simple with usually.

learn.title: Simple sentences: subject + verb + object
learn.html:
English has an almost fixed order: subject + verb + object. If one part is missing, the sentence is incomplete.

SubjectVerbObject
Joannaeatsorganic food
Ryanrecyclesbottles and jars
Martha and Leowastea lot of water

Adverbs (usually, always, often) go between the subject and the verb: I usually ride a bike.

watch.wrong: I always the computer turn off.
watch.right: I always turn off the computer.
Some cars use too much gas.
watch.why: The object is missing: what do they use?

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• What are you doing to help? — ask what someone does for a cause.
  • What are you doing these days? — I'm studying at college. — ask about someone's current period.
  • At the moment, … / Right now, … — talk about what is happening now.
  • Can I call you later? I'm eating dinner. — say that you are busy.
  • How green are you? — title of the unit quiz.
  • Can I get a ride with you? — ask for a lift.
  • Good luck! — wish someone luck.
  • Not too bad. / Well done! — answers about how you are, or a congratulation.
  • Don't waste water / electricity. — green tips with the imperative.

reading.title: A different week
paragraphs: Hi Pablo! How are you? I'm writing this email from my apartment in Guadalajara. It's Saturday morning and I'm drinking coffee on the balcony. It's a relaxing morning!

This week is different. I usually work in an office downtown, but this week I'm working at home because the office is closed. My boss is in Oaxaca. She's visiting her family. My office is usually busy and noisy, so working at home is nice.

My neighbors are very green. They always recycle bottles and paper, and they ride bikes to work. Today they're cleaning up trash in the park with some friends. My brother Luis is stressed. He usually plays soccer on Saturdays, but today he's studying for an exam. He doesn't like it!
I want to be more green too. I take the bus now, and I turn off the lights when I leave. Call me this afternoon. I'm not busy!
